title: After Trump’s Rout, Will Global Trade Keep Defying Politics?
text:
After Trump’s Rout, Will Global Trade Keep Defying Politics?

Tom Miller

Gavekal Research | 10 Nov 2026

War and tariffs have knocked President Donald Trump and the Republican Party off track, but global trade continues to defy these geopolitical headwinds. This is not simply an artifact of higher prices for oil and microchips: goods trade volume is growing at its fastest pace in 15 years, excluding the post-Covid rebound. The expansion is driven both by strong global appetite for artificial-intelligence equipment and by exporters finding alternative markets and adapting to supply-chain disruptions.The World Trade Organization forecasts that trade growth will accelerate further in 2027. The outlook is not without risks: if the AI boom turns to bust, trade growth will slow sharply in both volume and value terms. A political backlash against Chinese exports, which could reach a scarcely believable US$4.5trn in 2026, would compound the slowdown. Yet the world will struggle to break its addiction to Chinese goods, while a sustained AI investment boom would provide continued demand.
